recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-34391; any future change to the extension definitions themselves should be handled in the Extension Pack or a new tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-34391 reported that the Questionnaire item-type definition for type quantity referenced questionnaire-unit even though that extension is constrained to integer and decimal items, and requested quantity guidance that points to questionnaire-unitOption and questionnaire-unitValueSet instead.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 2b05abaa326cecce039b86ce1ad0ceb1acbb10c7, which changed source/questionnaire/codesystem-item-type.xml from questionnaire-unit to questionnaire-unitOption/questionnaire-unitValueSet for the quantity concept. A later same-family FHIR-28132 commit, e096aeb964003e83e479bbbe5b7991b8c825ca4a, refined the text and added the matching decimal/integer questionnaire-unit guidance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps Questionnaire active and lists the active item-type value set, which composes http://hl7.org/fhir/item-type from the neighboring Questionnaire code system. The current Extension Pack definitions constrain questionnaire-unit to integer/decimal and questionnaire-unitOption/questionnaire-unitValueSet to quantity. Later FHIR-37468 and FHIR-41195 source commits changed the quantity datatype wording toward SimpleQuantity but retained the corrected unit-extension guidance. FHIR-I SDC minutes list FHIR-34391 as Persuasive, and community searches found no contrary discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current quantity definition in source/questionnaire/codesystem-item-type.xml references questionnaire-unitOption and questionnaire-unitValueSet, the decimal and integer definitions appropriately reference questionnaire-unit, and no current source file under source/ contains the obsolete quantity wording that caused the issue.
